Word Stress

Session 4, part 1 of 2.

The rule

French rhythm is a machine gun. Every syllable the same length, the same force, rat-a-tat-a-tat. English rhythm is Morse code. Strong and weak alternate, and one syllable in each word stands out from the rest.

Amé-ri-que  →  three even syllables
A-ME-ri-ca  →  four syllables, one of them said, three thrown away

What "stressed" actually means: the stressed syllable is higher, stronger, longer. Not louder on its own. Higher in pitch, stronger in force, longer in time, all three at once.

And the other three? They go to the schwa: where the stress is not, the vowel goes to nothing. America is /əˈmerɪkə/, and two of its four vowels are the sound named after nothing.

The mark in the dictionary. When you look a word up you will see /ˈ/ before a syllable. That is the stress, and it goes in front of the syllable you lean on: computer is /kəmˈpjuːtə/, so the stress is on pu. On this page we use CAPITALS instead, because they are easier to see: computer.

1 · Listening exercise

Before you learn any rule, learn to hear the shape of a word. ● is a strong syllable, • is a weak one. Say the word out loud, then pick its rhythm.

2 · The stress is not in the word. It is in the ending.

Find the ending. Count back. Done.
You do not need to know the word. You need to know the ending.
-ic(s)
-ical
-ity
-ive		 Stress the syllable just before it.
robotics · mechanics · hydraulics · automatic · electric · magnetic · electricity · productivity · conductivity · capacity · velocity
-ion
-ial
-ious
-uate		 Stress the syllable just before it.
automation · insulation · regulation · connection · calibration · distribution · transmission · production · installation · industrial

3 · The procedure

Four steps. It works on words you have never seen.

pro · duc · ti · vi · ty
1Find the ending. Here it is -ity.
2That ending is in the "just before" list.
3Count back one syllable from the ending: ti.
4Say it higher, stronger, longer, and throw the other four away.
productivity   ••●••

Try it on a word you may not know: permittivity. Ending -ity, count back one, and you get permittivity. You may have never said that word before and you now know how to pr pronunce it
